schema_note: Cross-cutting supporting evidence -- fee benchmarks, market-structure surveys, and similar reference material that applies across countries or regions rather than to one segment of one country's data file. Deliberately kept separate from the per-country {code}.json files (segments/sources[]/scorecard) so it can be maintained and cited independently of any single market, then optionally attached to a client report as an appendix via picker.html's 'Attach supporting evidence' picker. Does not feed scoring automatically -- see individual entries' related_dimensions for where a figure could inform analyst judgment on a scorecard dimension. Added 2026-07-27, per Peter's request to gather this kind of material in a separate area rather than forcing it onto individual countries.

entries.title: Mercer Global Asset Manager Fee Survey
entries.source: Mercer, Global Asset Manager Fee Survey (5th+ edition)
entries.access: Historically complimentary at Mercer Global Investment Forums; current editions also accessible via free MercerInsight Community registration ('MercerInsight Trends')
entries.summary: Country/region median investment management fee benchmarks, blended across asset classes: Canada ~0.30%, UK ~0.40%, Europe ~0.50%, Asia ~0.75%, Emerging Markets ~0.89%.
entries.note: All-asset-class blended averages, not broken out by specific strategy or mandate size. Country/region granularity is this survey's key strength relative to bfinance's IMF Series (see below) -- but the two use different methodologies (survey responses vs. real quoted fees) and shouldn't be treated as directly reconcilable line items.

entries.title: bfinance Investment Management Fees series ("IMF Series")
entries.source: bfinance, "Pricing Pressure in the Turbulent Twenties" (2026 edition; biennial IMF Series, prior editions 2019, 2021-22, 2023-24)
entries.access: Free download via email-gated landing page (bfinance website)
entries.summary: Real quoted-mandate fee benchmarks by specific strategy and mandate size, with quartile ranges and multi-year trend lines. No country axis -- fees are pooled globally, not broken out by client domicile.

entries.note: Based on real quoted mandate fees, not survey responses -- a different and complementary methodology to Mercer's country-benchmark survey above. Has no country/region granularity, so cannot substitute for Mercer's figures; best read alongside Mercer, not instead of it. A November 2024 bfinance poll of 300+ investors found roughly 40%+ believed like-for-like private equity fees had fallen, despite little stated-term compression showing in bfinance's own PE figures -- a perception-vs-data gap worth flagging if PE fee compression comes up with a client.
